newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Senior Cambodian royalist attacks premier.
newsitem.headline: Senior Cambodian royalist attacks premier.

text.p: A senior royalist party member on Tuesday criticised Prince Norodom Ranariddh's leadership, saying the co-premier's policies could lead Cambodia to disaster.

Minister of State Ung Phan urged other members of the FUNCINPEC party to endorse a statement "rejecting" the prince's authority. Ung Phan is a former comrade-in-arms of Ranariddh's rival in the coalition government, co-Premier Hun Sen,
The statement was issued in the name of FUNCINPEC members of parliament and national council members, but Ung Phan's name was the only one listed.
The statement said Ranariddh's alleged inconsistency as a leader could "lead the nation towards great disaster."
The statement said supporters rejected "the dangerous leadership of Norodom Ranariddh as of from today" and would work to strengthen relations between the coalition government parties.

The statement said political instability had resulted from Ranariddh's threats at a March 1996 party congress to withdraw from the coalition government with the Cambodian People's Party (CPP), dissolve parliament and hold early elections.
Ranariddh was overseas and his reaction was not known, but the CPP issued a statement backing Ung Phan's statement.

Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC formed an uneasy coalition with the CPP after the U.N.-run elections in 1993. Tensions have been particulalry high since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on an opposition rally led by FUNCINPEC ally Sam Rainsy.
Ung Phan was jailed in 1990 for trying to form an independent political group while a minister in the CPP government of Hun Sen.
